chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) begin the prayer, so he raised his hands near his face and faced the Qiblah with the palms of his hands.
ai.seo_question: How did the Imams raise their hands during the opening of prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the specific sunnah of raising hands (raf' al-yadayn) to the level of the face during the opening takbir, a practice emphasized in Shia jurisprudence to denote humility and focus. The detail of facing the Qiblah with the palms underscores the physical orientation of the worshipper, linking bodily posture directly to spiritual presence (khushu') before Allah.
